facts.statement: The genus Weejasperaspis was described by White in 1978.
Weejasperaspis lived during the Early Devonian period.
This extinct acanthothoracid placoderm was found in the Wee Jasper reef in eastern New South Wales, Australia.
facts.quote: Weejasperaspis is an extinct acanthothoracid placoderm found in the Wee Jasper reef, of the Early Devonian-aged Murrumbidgee Group in eastern New South Wales, Australia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Weejasperaspis gavini.
facts.quote: the type species is W. gavini

facts.statement: Weejasperaspis is distinguished from other acanthothoracids by having a short, triangular-shaped median dorsal crest.
facts.quote: Weejasperaspis differs from other acanthothoracids in that the median dorsal crest is short, and triangular-shaped

facts.statement: Fossils of Weejasperaspis are known only from a dorsal plate and ossified eyeballs.
facts.quote: Like Murrindalaspis, it is only known from a dorsal plate and ossified eyeballs

facts.statement: Weejasperaspis belongs to the class Placodermi.
The genus Weejasperaspis is classified within the family Weejasperaspidae.
Weejasperaspis lived between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago during the Emsian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 393.47 million years ago)
